reason: Merger arbitrage relies on qualitative checklists for bid credibility, binding status, major shareholders, and downside risk sizing rather than mechanical daily-bar rules.

universe.description: ASX-listed takeover targets (not US daily-bar testable)

setup.rule: Assess binding vs non-binding, bidder history, funding, major shareholder support
setup.quote: first thing we're primarily interested in is you know how credible is the bid in terms of you know things like is it binding or non-binding who's the bidder is it funded

entry.rule: Buy at discount to bid after announcement if risk score supports position size
entry.quote: we might have on a one-quarter position size

stop.rule: Exit if deal fails at pre-bid low adjusted for market conditions
stop.quote: if the transaction falls over what's the likely lowest level that this stock is going to trade at and usually as a starting point we'd use like the you know the three or six months low prior to the bid

exits.rule: Hold to completion or trim at 10% premium to current bid or when risk score drops
exits.quote: usually if we saw a situation where the current share price is 10 above whatever the current best announced bid is in the market usually we'd be taking some uh off the table at that point

sizing.rule: Score deal 0-100; full size at 100, min quarter size, risk = (entry - worst-case exit) / portfolio risk pct
sizing.quote: we're sort of scoring that out of a hundred so we think of of 100 as being a full risk position size

market_filter.rule: Prefer uncorrelated M&A situations over broad market beta
market_filter.quote: m a you know tends to be uncorrelated um you know uh for the most part to broader markets

ambiguities.issue: Transcript covers Australian ASX deals only; no US stock rules given
ambiguities.assumption: Cannot map to daily US equity engine
